brenda-smith.text: Endorsed by the East Whittier Education Association (teachers' union) and California School Employees Association Chapter 87.

Smith says that when cuts are necessary they "should begin as far away from classrooms as possible," with the district examining administrative staffing and district-level spending before reducing teachers or raising class sizes.

source.title: Brenda Smith for EWCSD: Smaller, Manageable Class Sizes

brenda-smith.text: Smith's priority: "Adequately staff our schools before expanding nonessential administration." She says custodians, aides and other classified staff are essential and the district should examine why classified positions are hard to fill, including pay and hours.

source.title: Brenda Smith for EWCSD: Protecting School-Site Staffing

brenda-smith.text: Smith wants budgets to explain what money pays for and why, and says that when year-end results differ substantially from projections used for staffing decisions, the board should publicly examine and explain the difference.

source.title: Brenda Smith for EWCSD: Financial Transparency

brenda-smith.text: Smith says that if the district finishes a year with substantially more resources than projected after staffing cuts, the board should ask whether those funds could have supported classroom positions, classified staff, programs or better compensation.

source.title: Brenda Smith for EWCSD: Using Resources for Today's Students

brenda-smith.text: Smith says board members should question administrators' recommendations, hear teachers and parents who challenge them, and postpone decisions when needed rather than cast "automatic votes."

source.title: Brenda Smith for EWCSD: Thoughtful Decisions, Not Automatic Votes

brenda-smith.text: Smith supports live broadcasts of EWCSD board meetings with recordings kept publicly available afterward.

source.title: Brenda Smith for EWCSD: Open Access to School Board Meetings

brenda-smith.text: Smith says the superintendent should have clear, measurable goals, and the community should be able to see how student achievement factors into the superintendent's evaluation.

source.title: Brenda Smith for EWCSD: Accountability at Every Level
